title: Implement Graceful Shutdown with Signal Handling
description: Adds support for handling SIGTERM/SIGINT, stops accepting new requests, waits for in‑flight requests, and closes the server cleanly. Provides a configurable shutdown timeout and optional cleanup hooks, improving reliability in containerized and production deployments.
testCases: Signal handling: send SIGTERM to a running server, verify it stops accepting new connections, allows existing request to finish, and exits with code 0 within the configured timeout
Timeout fallback: start a long‑running request, trigger SIGTERM, set shutdown timeout shorter than request duration, verify server forces shutdown after timeout and logs a warning
acceptance: When the process receives SIGTERM or SIGINT, the framework stops accepting new connections, waits up to the configured timeout for all in‑flight requests to complete, executes any registered cleanup callbacks, and then exits cleanly. If the timeout expires, the server forces shutdown and logs an appropriate warning. All test cases pass and no unhandled promise rejections occur.
reason: Production environments (e.g., Kubernetes, Docker) require graceful termination to avoid dropped requests and resource leaks. Implementing this feature dramatically increases reliability and makes yantraverse suitable for zero‑downtime deployments, a critical business need.
